newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish unemployment should fall in March -minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish unemployment should fall in March -minister.

text.p: Polish unemployment, which fell to 13.5 percent of the workforce in January from 13.6 percent in December, should stay flat in February and start falling from March, the labour minister said on Friday.
"The unemployment rate should stay unchanged until March and then the situation should significantly improve," Tadeusz Zielinski told a news conference.
He also said that the number of unemployed fell by 23,200 in January to 2.34 million against 2.72 million in January 1996. @

But president of the National Employment Office, also present, said that from January some groups of pensioners, graduates and people undergoing vocational training in labour offices were excluded from official unemployed statistics.
"The number of unemployed was cut by 61,000 under the January bill that excluded some groups from statistics of unemployed," Andrzej Pilat said.
